_doc: High or critical advisories the audit floor gate (check-audit-floor.mjs) accepts on purpose, keyed by package directory (the keys are also the only directories the script runs from). Fields: `ghsa` the advisory id as `npm audit` reports it (the GHSA id, or `npm-<source id>` for an advisory without a GitHub URL; the gate's FAIL line names it); `package` the vulnerable package (an entry matches on ghsa AND package); `range` the vulnerable range exactly as `npm audit` reported it when the entry was reviewed (when npm audit reports a different range the advisory has moved, usually because a patch was published, and the gate FAILs until a human re-reviews the entry; it also FAILs an entry when npm reports a reachable fix, `fixAvailable` true or a non-major parent change); `why` the reasoning (why no override can fix it); `revisit` the condition that retires the entry. A matching advisory prints as `accepted` and does not fail the gate; an entry the audit no longer reports, or now reports below high, prints as `stale`, for a human to remove in a reviewed PR. A repeated (ghsa, package) pair stops the gate (exit 2). The scan never edits this file. Tests point the script at their own copy through ACCEPTED_ADVISORIES_FILE. Reasoning: docs/automation/daily-upgrade-scan.md, 'Audit floor gate'.

mobile.why: Stack-exhaustion DoS through deeply nested brace patterns. Every published braces (<= 3.0.3, the latest) is affected and the advisory lists no patched version, so no override can lift it. In the production tree it arrives through metro's micromatch (build-time tooling under @sentry/react-native and expo), never in the app bundle, and only parses patterns from our own config. The GitHub alert was dismissed by the owner on 2026-10-18 (#924).
mobile.revisit: When braces publishes a release the advisory names as patched: add an override (or take the upstream bump) and remove this entry in the same PR.

mobile.why: RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification accepts extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements. Every published node-forge (<= 1.4.0, the latest) is affected and the advisory lists no patched version. It arrives through @expo/code-signing-certificates (expo-updates and @expo/cli), which this app does not use: EAS Update code signing is not configured. The GitHub alert was dismissed by the owner on 2026-10-18 (#924).
mobile.revisit: When node-forge publishes a release the advisory names as patched, or Expo drops node-forge: add an override (or take the upstream bump) and remove this entry in the same PR.
